packages.title: UK 2023 consumption carbon footprint 699 MtCO2e QA
facts: Defra estimates the UK consumption-based greenhouse-gas footprint at 699 MtCO2e in 2023.
The estimate is for consumption rather than territorial emissions.
It covers supply-chain emissions associated with UK resident consumption.
It includes direct household fossil-fuel emissions.
The national estimate is not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: UK carbon footprint 4 percent annual fall QA
facts: The UK carbon footprint fell 4% between 2022 and 2023.
The percentage change is calculated from unrounded estimates.
The 2023 footprint remains below the 2007 peak.
The comparison is annual and consumption-based.
No property-level change is inferred from the national trend.

packages.title: UK consumption footprint 10 tCO2e per capita QA
facts: UK consumption-based GHG emissions were estimated at 10 tCO2e per person in 2023.
The per-capita figure fell 5% from 2022.
It was 37% below the 2004 peak of 16 tCO2e per person.
Per-capita statistics use population as a denominator.
An average per-person figure is not a parcel emission value.

packages.title: Imported emissions majority-share QA
facts: Imported emissions accounted for more than half of the UK consumption footprint in 2023.
Imported emissions are estimated through supply-chain modelling.
They include emissions occurring outside the UK.
They differ from territorial emissions produced within UK borders.
The imported share cannot be assigned to an individual parcel without additional evidence.

packages.title: China import embedded-emissions share QA
facts: In 2023, emissions embedded in imports from China accounted for 25% of emissions from imports.
They accounted for 13% of the UK's total consumption footprint.
The statistic concerns imported goods and services.
It is consumption-account evidence rather than territorial inventory evidence.
The country-of-origin share is not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: England 2023 consumption footprint 587 MtCO2e QA
facts: England's consumption-based GHG footprint was estimated at 587 MtCO2e in 2023.
It fell 3% between 2022 and 2023.
It remained below the 2007 peak of 826 MtCO2e.
The estimate is consumption-based and includes overseas supply-chain emissions.
The England total is not a parcel-level value.

packages.title: UK 2023 carbon-dioxide footprint 548 MtCO2 QA
facts: The UK carbon-dioxide consumption footprint was estimated at 548 MtCO2 in 2023.
It fell 4% from 2022.
This measure covers CO2 rather than all greenhouse gases.
MtCO2 must not be silently substituted for MtCO2e.
The national CO2 footprint is not parcel-specific.

packages.title: England 2023 carbon-dioxide footprint 461 MtCO2 QA
facts: England's carbon-dioxide consumption footprint was estimated at 461 MtCO2 in 2023.
It fell 3% from 2022.
The measure is restricted to carbon dioxide.
It differs from the broader GHG footprint expressed in CO2e.
No parcel CO2 value is inferred.

packages.title: Consumption territorial production trend-boundary QA
facts: Since 1996, the UK consumption footprint decreased by 15% through 2023.
Territorial emissions fell by 50% over the same comparison stated by Defra.
Production-based emissions decreased by 42% over the same comparison.
The three series use different accounting boundaries.
Their trend percentages must not be mixed as if they measured the same scope.

packages.title: Imported embedded emissions 371 MtCO2e QA
facts: Embedded GHG emissions from imports totalled 371 MtCO2e in 2023.
They were 21% below their 2007 peak.
The estimate is part of the consumption account.
It is model-based supply-chain evidence.
Imported embedded emissions are not direct measurements at UK parcels.

packages.title: UK-produced domestic consumption emissions 206 MtCO2e QA
facts: Emissions associated with UK-produced goods and services consumed domestically were 206 MtCO2e in 2023.
They fell from 208 MtCO2e in 2022.
They accounted for 29% of total consumption-based emissions in 2023.
This component is distinct from imported and direct-household components.
The component total is not a parcel allocation.

packages.title: Direct household consumption emissions 122 MtCO2e QA
facts: Direct UK household emissions were estimated at 122 MtCO2e in 2023.
They were 25% lower than in 1996.
The component includes household fossil-fuel use such as heating and personal vehicles.
Direct household emissions are one component of the consumption footprint.
The national household total does not identify emissions from a specific dwelling.

packages.title: Household heating emissions 61 MtCO2e QA
facts: Heating-related direct household emissions were estimated at 61 MtCO2e in 2023.
They were 65 MtCO2e in 2022.
Heating emissions fluctuate with winter temperatures.
The figure belongs to the consumption-account direct-household component.
No individual home's heating emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Consumption footprint MRIO modelling QA
facts: Defra's consumption-account estimates use a Multi-Regional Input-Output model developed by the University of Leeds.
The model combines economic activity, trade, supply-chain and GHG information.
Further analysis derives England-level results.
Model outputs are estimates rather than direct parcel measurements.
The modelling basis must be retained in provenance.

packages.title: Overseas embedded-emissions uncertainty QA
facts: Defra states overseas embedded emissions are more difficult to estimate than emissions generated within the UK.
Internationally recognised methods are used for the estimates.
Overseas estimates carry greater uncertainty than territorial emissions.
Uncertainty is a methodological property and must not be hidden.
High-level uncertainty does not justify inventing parcel values.

packages.title: Consumption-account exports exclusion QA
facts: UK-produced goods that are exported are excluded from the UK consumption footprint.
The exclusion follows the residence-consumption purpose of the account.
Exports relate to consumption outside the UK or England.
Consumption and production accounting therefore have different boundaries.
Export exclusions must be preserved in cross-source comparisons.

packages.title: Consumption-account LULUCF exclusion QA
facts: Defra states land use, land-use change and forestry emissions in the UK and abroad are excluded from this consumption footprint.
The exclusion differs from territorial inventory treatment of LULUCF.
Accounting-boundary differences can materially affect comparisons.
LULUCF values must not be added without compatible scope.
No land-parcel carbon value is inferred from the consumption account.

packages.title: ONS three greenhouse-gas accounting bases QA
facts: ONS distinguishes residence, territorial and consumption approaches to UK greenhouse-gas emissions.
Residence-based emissions align with National Accounts concepts.
Territorial emissions concern emissions within UK borders.
Consumption emissions include supply-chain emissions associated with resident consumption.
The accounting bases are not interchangeable.

packages.title: Seven greenhouse-gas species scope QA
facts: The UK greenhouse-gas scope includes carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide.
It also includes hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride.
Totals may be expressed in carbon-dioxide equivalent.
Individual gas quantities and CO2e totals must remain distinct.
A national gas-species dataset is not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: ONS current versus provisional atmospheric-emissions edition QA
facts: ONS provides both current and provisional editions of the atmospheric GHG dataset.
The current edition provides data for all economic sectors.
The provisional edition provides top-level estimates.
The dataset covers around 130 SIC 2007 industry groups in the current edition.
Edition status must be preserved when comparing values.
